generated_video_script.full_script:
[INÍCIO DO ROTEIRO - 7.053 caracteres]

Have you ever tried to plug a USB cable and it wouldn't go in?

You turned it, tried again. Still wouldn't go in.

Turned it one more time. And suddenly, it went in.

You're not crazy. Physics explains why.

The USB was designed to be plugged in one way. But in practice, it has two possible orientations. The problem is that you never know which one is correct.

This is called the 'USB orientation problem.' And it's one of the greatest mysteries of modern engineering.

But here is the truth: USB is not the only culprit. Power outlets, audio cables, even some chargers have the same problem.

The solution? USB-C. It was designed to be plugged in any way. And that's why it's replacing all other cables.

So next time you struggle with a USB, remember: it's not you. It's physics.

And physics, as we know, is relentless.
